newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish liberals say UK vote pressures Denmark on EU.
newsitem.headline: Danish liberals say UK vote pressures Denmark on EU.

text.p: Denmark's leading opposition Liberal party said on Friday that Labour's victory in Britain could mean increased pressure on Euro-sceptical Denmark to conform with European Union policies.

"There is no doubt that we are going to see a more positive British policy within the European Union. The Labour win has paved the way for a swift completion of the intergovernmental conference on Europe's future," Liberal leader Uffe Ellemann-Jensen told the Ritzau news agency.
Ellemann-Jensen, a staunch pro-European, is a former foreign minister and, according to opinion polls, his party is likely to head a centre-right government after elections due by September 1998.

"This will put pressure on Denmark's EU policy. Denmark has in the past been able to hide itself behind British Euro-scepticism to a certain degree, now we will have to sort out exactly where we stand on European issues," he said.
Danes, traditionally cool toward European integration, rejected the Maastricht Treaty outright in a 1992 referendum.
Voters grudgingly approved the treaty the following year on condition that Denmark opt out of economic and monetary union and joint defence, policing and citizenship arrangements.
